expiry.rulesIntro: Expiry is auto-filled from the date of monitoring plus the period below, and can be changed on any report (for example, to the next monitoring date the assessor recommends). Statutory periods come from the cited DOSH/DOE regulation; typical periods depend on the client's licence, approval conditions or CHRA findings and should be confirmed per client.
expiry.waitingForDate: Enter the date of monitoring to calculate the expiry.
expiry.unconfirmedNoticeTitle: {count, plural, =1 {1 report needs its date of monitoring} other {# reports need their date of monitoring}}
expiry.unconfirmedNoticeHint: These dates were filled in automatically, so their expiry may be wrong. Key in the real date to fix it.
expiry.legendStatutory: The period is written in the regulation. The exact clause is shown, and the source link opens the regulation.
expiry.legendTypical: The usual period in practice. The real one is in the client's DOE licence, approval conditions or assessor's report, so check it for each client.
expiry.legendNoExpiry: There is no legal renewal period, so no expiry is filled in. Review it when the work changes, or add an expiry by hand if the client's own programme sets one.
expiry.actionHint: The report stops showing as due for renewal for every staff member. You can undo this from the report page.

map.notFoundTitle: Not found in the free map search
map.notFoundBody: Small companies often aren't in free map data, and we won't guess a look-alike. Get the exact spot from Google Maps instead. It takes a few seconds:
map.guide1: Open Google Maps (button below) and find the company.
map.guide2: On a computer, right-click the exact building and click the numbers at the top to copy them. On a phone, tap Share → Copy link.
map.guide3: Paste it in the box above and press Use this location. You can also just click the map.
